# verda vm

> Verda CLI **v1.10.0** · [other versions](https://github.com/verda-cloud/verda-cli/tags)

Manage virtual machines

Create and manage Verda virtual machine instances.

Aliases: `instance`, `instances`

Subcommands:

- [`verda vm action`](#verda-vm-action): Perform actions on a VM instance
- [`verda vm availability`](#verda-vm-availability): Show available instance types with specs and pricing
- [`verda vm create`](#verda-vm-create): Create a VM instance
- [`verda vm delete`](#verda-vm-delete): Delete a VM instance
- [`verda vm describe`](#verda-vm-describe): Show detailed information about a VM instance
- [`verda vm hibernate`](#verda-vm-hibernate): Hibernate a VM instance (deprecated, will be removed in a future version)
- [`verda vm list`](#verda-vm-list): List VM instances
- [`verda vm shutdown`](#verda-vm-shutdown): Shutdown a VM instance
- [`verda vm start`](#verda-vm-start): Start a VM instance

## verda vm action

Perform actions on a VM instance

Select a VM instance and perform an action: start, shutdown,
force shutdown, hibernate (deprecated), or delete.

Hibernate is deprecated and will be removed in a future version.
It discontinues compute and retains volumes. Retained volumes continue billing.

**Usage**

```text
verda vm action [flags]
```

**Flags**

```text
      --action string           Action to perform: start, shutdown, force_shutdown, hibernate (deprecated), delete
      --id string               Instance ID to act on
      --wait                    Wait for the operation to complete (default true)
      --wait-timeout duration   Maximum time to wait for the operation (default 5m0s)
      --yes                     Skip confirmation for destructive actions (required in agent mode)
```

**Examples**

```bash
# Interactive: select instance then action
verda vm action

# Specify instance ID
verda vm action --id abc-123

# Run action and wait for completion
verda vm action --id abc-123 --wait

# Non-interactive (agent mode)
verda --agent vm action --id abc-123 --action shutdown
verda --agent vm action --id abc-123 --action delete --yes
```

## verda vm availability

Show available instance types with specs and pricing

Show currently available instance types with full specs, pricing,
and datacenter locations. This helps you find what you can launch
right now and how much it costs.

**Usage**

```text
verda vm availability [flags]
```

Aliases: `avail`

**Flags**

```text
      --kind string       Filter by kind: gpu or cpu
      --location string   Filter by location code (e.g., FIN-01)
      --spot              Show spot pricing and availability
      --type string       Filter by instance type (e.g., 1V100.6V)
```

**Examples**

```bash
# Show all available instance types
verda vm availability

# Filter by location
verda vm availability --location FIN-01

# Check a specific instance type
verda vm availability --type 1V100.6V

# GPU instances only
verda vm availability --kind gpu

# Spot pricing
verda vm availability --spot

# JSON output for scripting
verda vm availability -o json
```

## verda vm create

Create a VM instance

Create a Verda VM instance. Without flags, launches an interactive
wizard. Use --from to pre-fill settings from a saved template.
Flags passed alongside --from override the template values.

Templates are created with "verda template create" and stored
as YAML files under ~/.verda/templates/vm/.

**Usage**

```text
verda vm create [flags]
```

**Flags**

```text
      --contract string                        Billing contract: pay_as_go, long_term, or spot. Long-term durations are not exposed by POST /v1/instances.
      --coupon string                          Coupon code to apply to the instance creation
      --description string                     Human-readable description; defaults to the hostname
      --existing-volume strings                Existing volume ID to attach; repeat the flag for multiple volumes
      --from string[=" "]                      Create from a saved template; use alone to pick from list
      --hostname string                        Hostname for the new VM
      --instance-type string                   Instance type, for example 1V100.6V
      --is-spot                                Request a spot instance
      --kind string                            Compute class: gpu or cpu
      --location string                        Location code, for example FIN-01 (default "FIN-01")
      --os string                              OS image slug or an existing detached OS volume ID
      --os-volume-name string                  Name of the OS volume to create; requires --os-volume-size
      --os-volume-on-spot-discontinue string   Spot discontinue policy for the OS volume: keep_detached, move_to_trash, or delete_permanently; requires --os-volume-size and --is-spot
      --os-volume-size int                     Size of the OS volume in GiB; required if any other --os-volume-* flag is set
      --pricing string                         Pricing mode string accepted by the API, for example FIXED_PRICE
      --ssh-key strings                        SSH key ID to inject into the instance; repeat the flag for multiple keys
      --startup-script string                  Startup script ID to attach
      --storage-name string                    Name of the optional additional storage volume; defaults to <hostname>-storage
      --storage-on-spot-discontinue string     Spot discontinue policy for the optional additional storage volume
      --storage-size int                       Size of the optional additional storage volume in GiB
      --storage-type string                    Type of the optional additional storage volume (default "NVMe")
      --volume stringArray                     Create and attach a new volume using name:size:type[:location[:on-spot-discontinue]]
      --wait                                   Wait for the operation to complete (default true)
      --wait-timeout duration                  Maximum time to wait for the operation (default 5m0s)
```

**Examples**

```bash
# Interactive wizard
verda vm create

# From a saved template (only prompts for hostname + confirm)
verda vm create --from gpu-training
verda vm create --from gpu-training --hostname my-vm

# Pick template from list
verda vm create --from

# From a template file
verda vm create --from ./my-template.yaml

# From a template, override specific fields with flags
verda vm create --from gpu-training --location FIN-03
verda vm create --from gpu-training --hostname my-vm --os-volume-size 200

# Non-interactive with all flags
verda vm create \
--kind gpu \
--instance-type 1V100.6V \
--location FIN-01 \
--os ubuntu-24.04-cuda-13.0-open-docker \
--os-volume-size 100 \
--hostname gpu-runner \
--ssh-key ssh_key_123
```

## verda vm delete

Delete a VM instance

**Usage**

```text
verda vm delete <instance-id> [flags]
```

Aliases: `rm`

**Flags**

```text
      --all                     Target all instances (use with --status/--hostname to filter)
      --hostname string         Filter by hostname glob pattern, requires --all (e.g., "test-*")
      --id string               Instance ID (alternative to positional argument)
      --status string           Filter by status, requires --all (e.g., running, offline)
      --wait                    Wait for the operation to complete (default true)
      --wait-timeout duration   Maximum time to wait for the operation (default 5m0s)
      --with-volumes            Also delete all attached volumes (delete only); without it the OS volume survives detached and keeps billing
      --yes                     Skip confirmation for destructive actions
```

**Examples**

```bash
# Delete a VM instance a specific instance
verda vm delete inst-abc-123

# Interactive: select from list
verda vm delete

# Batch: delete all matching instances
verda vm delete --all --status offline

# Batch: delete instances matching hostname pattern
verda vm delete --all --hostname "test-*"

# Batch: combine filters (AND logic)
verda vm delete --all --status offline --hostname "test-*"

# Batch delete with volumes
verda vm delete --all --status offline --with-volumes --yes
```

```bash

```
